title: Otis and the Wiggly Wonders
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a sunny little hollow by a river that made happy noises, lived an otter named Otis. Otis was a very happy otter, and he loved to draw. He had a small notepad made of smooth, flat leaves and a little pencil he’d found near the berry bushes. He would sit by the riverbank, dip his paw in the cool, clear water for a bit of ‘ink’ to make his drawings shiny. Every day, Otis practiced his art. He drew the tall grasses that swayed like dancers, he drew the smooth, grey stones that skipped across the water, and he drew Sunny the puppy, who was always chasing colorful dragonflies.

But here's the thing that sometimes made Otis sigh: his drawings were… well, they were a little bit wobbly. The grasses didn't stand up straight; they leaned and wiggled, like they were whispering secrets. The stones, meant to be round, looked more like happy little sausages. And Sunny, bless his fluffy tail, often ended up with a tail that wiggled so much it threatened to wiggle right off the page! Sunny, however, thought Otis’s drawings were the best. "Woof! That's a wiggly fish, Otis!" he'd bark, wagging his tail so hard he stirred up a little cloud of dust. And Otis would just smile, because Sunny’s happy barks made his heart feel warm, like a sunbeam.

This is the part where things start to change. Until one day, a special announcement floated down from the oldest oak tree at the edge of the hollow. It was a little scroll, tied with a vine, from Miss Willow, the wise old owl. "My dear riverside friends," her gentle voice echoed, "we are having a special art competition! Let us see the wonderful things you can create!"

Otis’s whiskers twitched with excitement. An art competition! He imagined his drawing of Sunny, perfectly straight and sharp, winning a big, shiny blue ribbon. He could picture it now, hanging proudly in his cozy den. But then he looked down at his notepad. All his lines were so… wiggly. The grasses did a little dance, the sausages looked ready to roll away, and Sunny’s tail had a mind of its own. "Oh dear," he mumbled, his smile drooping a little. "How can I win with wobbly art?"

Because of that, Otis decided he needed some very special help. He found a long, straight twig and tried to use it as a ruler for his drawings. But the twig kept slipping and sliding in the damp river water. *Swoosh!* One minute the grasses were leaning, the next they looked like they were doing a clumsy little dance. "Oh bother and double bother," sighed Otis, his brow furrowed.

Because of that, he remembered Barnaby. Barnaby was a bear cub, and his important job was to sharpen pencils. Barnaby liked his pencils to have very specific points. Otis trotted over to Barnaby’s cozy den, which smelled of wood shavings and a hint of sweet honey. "Barnaby," Otis said politely, trying to keep his voice steady, "could you please sharpen my pencil? I need it to be very, very straight for the art competition."

Barnaby blinked his sleepy eyes. "Straight, you say?" He took Otis’s pencil, and *whirrrrrrr* went his little sharpener. But as the wood shavings fell, a tiny voice seemed to whisper from the pencil tip. "Perhaps," it chirped, "we should draw a rainbow today! A very swirly, colourful rainbow!"

Otis blinked, surprised. "A rainbow? But I wanted to draw Sunny. He's important for the competition."

Barnaby, ever busy, nodded and took another pencil. *Whirrrrrrr.* This one whispered, its voice deep and rumbling, "Or maybe a big, bumpy mountain! Mountains are very strong and straight!"

"A mountain?" Otis frowned, his tail giving a little flick of disappointment. "But Sunny is much more fun than a mountain. And he smiles a lot more."

Barnaby, with the best of intentions, kept sharpening. And each pencil seemed to have a new idea. One suggested a zig-zag fence, another a spiral staircase, and another a cloud that wanted to float away. Otis’s notepad was getting quite full of these peculiar suggestions, but his drawing of Sunny was no closer to being straight, let alone finished. He felt a little sad. It was like a tiny bubble in his chest.

Because of that, Otis put his pencil down with a soft *thump*. He looked at his wobbly drawings, and the jaunty zig-zag fences, and the adventurous clouds. They weren't what he wanted to draw at all. He felt a bit glum, like a party balloon that had lost some of its air. Sunny, noticing Otis’s drooping whiskers, nudged his paw gently and gave a soft, questioning whine. The air around them seemed to grow a little quieter. He looked at his unfinished drawings, and his tummy felt a little wobbly too.

Then, as if by magic, Miss Willow swooped down from her perch on the oak tree. Her wide, feathery wings made no sound. Her eyes twinkled like little stars. "What's all this, Otis?" she asked kindly, her voice as soft as a gentle breeze. "You look as if you've lost your best skipping stone."

Otis sighed, a long, wavering sigh. "My drawings are too wobbly, Miss Willow," he confessed. "I want them to be straight and perfect, like everyone else's. I'll never win like this."

Miss Willow smiled, a wide, knowing smile. "But Otis," she said softly, tilting her head, "your drawings aren't wobbly. They're lively! They have… character! They dance!" She picked up a smooth, flat stone and a piece of charcoal. "Watch," she whispered, leaning closer. She drew a circle, and then a dot inside it. "This," she chirped, "is me, looking out at the world." Then she drew a long, swooping line that curved and dipped gracefully across the stone. "And this," she continued, "is my flight path, winding through the trees." The line wasn't perfectly straight, oh no, but it was elegant and full of the joy of flying. "Sometimes," she explained, "the straightest path isn't the most interesting one, my dear."

She gently dipped Otis’s otter paw into the river water again. "Let your paw follow the shape, Otis," she said. "Don't fight it. Let it flow, like the river itself."

Otis tried. He held his pencil just as Miss Willow had shown him. He looked at Sunny, whose happy barks filled the air. His tail was a brown and white blur, wagging so hard it kicked up little puffs of dry earth. Otis felt the warmth of the sun on his fur. And he began to draw. This time, he didn't try to force the lines to be perfectly straight. He let his paw move naturally, capturing Sunny’s bouncy energy, the wild joy in his wagging tail, the happy, open curve of his smiling mouth. The lines were still a little wiggly, yes, but they weren't shaky or uncertain anymore. They were bold and full of life. They were *Otis*.

And wouldn't you know it, the drawing looked just like Sunny! It looked happy. It looked like *him*, the real Sunny. Otis held it up, and his heart felt light, like a little dandelion seed caught on the breeze.

Finally, the day of the art competition arrived. The animals gathered by the riverbank, and each presented their masterpiece. The other animals had drawn very straight, very neat pictures. There were perfectly round flowers and buildings that stood up like soldiers. But when they saw Otis’s drawing of Sunny, so full of life and joy and wonderful, happy wiggles, they all gasped with delight. Sunny himself barked with pure joy and wagged his tail so hard it looked like a brown and white blur! Miss Willow smiled, a very proud smile indeed, and awarded Otis a special ribbon. It wasn't a ribbon for straight lines, but for the most joyful, most wonderfully *alive* drawing of the day.

Ever since then, Otis still drew by the river, and his lines were still wonderfully wiggly. But now, he knew that his own special way of seeing the world, his own unique style, was perfectly, beautifully just right. And Sunny always had the best wiggly pictures to chase, and even to frame!
characters: Otis the otter, Sunny the puppy, Miss Willow
